blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Establish Social and Economic Welfare State
Inspired by US Constitution (Bill of Rights)

items: Distinguish between Writ Jurisdiction: Supreme Court (Article 32) is narrower than High Court (Article 226) as SC issues writs only for Fundamental Rights.
Remember that the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty regarding education for children aged 6-14 years.
Directive Principles are non-enforceable by courts, whereas Fundamental Rights are justiciable.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights are guaranteed under Part III (Articles 12 to 35) of the Indian Constitution.
Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, empowering citizens to move the Supreme Court directly.
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) under Part IV aim to establish a welfare state and are non-justiciable.
Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Article 51A via the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
